correctness.rationale: On K_m with a single attached ell-edge tail, independent clique feasible variables are vertices of a root-anchored clique Lipschitz polytope under strictly convex centered variance. Each such vertex has signed 0/1 clique levels. Pairwise graph-distance domination straightens every maximizing tail away from negative clique values; positive finite differences exclude the all-zero clique pattern. The remaining quadratic N(B+k)-(A-k)^2, k=0..m-1, has exact nearest-integer maximum at (m+ell(ell+2))/2. The boundary m=ell(ell+2)+3 ties k=m-2 and m-1 and yields all claimed equality types. Independent exact computations for m,ell=(3,3),(4,3),(5,4),(8,3) agree with the variance formula and enumeration. Universal validity comes from strict convexity and exact algebra, not finite sampling.
residual_risks: Finite rational checks cover selected small examples, not the full range. No published alternative theorem was inferred from generic spread theory.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The published clique-bouquet theorem glues several cliques at a single vertex, and the bridge theorem joins two cliques; neither covers serial paths of ell>=3 beyond the clique. Generic all-graph statements supply only inequalities/existence, not this sharp two-parameter formula.
